title: New Year Garland
statementMd:
As Gerald, Alexander, Sergey and Gennady are already busy with the usual New Year chores, Edward hastily decorates the New Year Tree. And any decent New Year Tree must be decorated with a good garland. Edward has lamps of $*m*$ colors and he wants to make a garland from them. That garland should represent a sequence whose length equals $*L*$. Edward's tree is $*n*$ layers high and Edward plans to hang the garland so as to decorate the first layer with the first $*l*_{1}$ lamps, the second layer — with the next $*l*_{2}$ lamps and so on. The last $*n*$-th layer should be decorated with the last $*l*_{*n*}$ lamps, ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e444352e6f3188286a54650b0cc918121525a492.png)

Edward adores all sorts of math puzzles, so he suddenly wondered: how many different ways to assemble the garland are there given that the both following two conditions are met:

1. Any two lamps that follow consecutively in the same layer should have different colors.
2. The sets of used colors in every two **neighbouring** layers must be different. We consider unordered sets (not multisets), where every color occurs no more than once. So the number of lamps of particular color does not matter.

Help Edward find the answer to this nagging problem or else he won't manage to decorate the Tree by New Year. You may consider that Edward has an unlimited number of lamps of each of $*m*$ colors and it is not obligatory to use all $*m*$ colors. The garlands are considered different if they differ in at least one position when represented as sequences. Calculate the answer modulo $*p*$.

## Input

The first line contains three integers $*n*$, $*m*$ and $*p*$ ($1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 10^{6}$, $2 ≤ *p* ≤ 10^{9}$) which are the number of the tree's layers, the number of the lamps' colors and module correspondingly. The next line contains $*n*$ integers $*l*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ 5000$, ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ba00472aa4924de40da7f039202523b7f0cf35f8.png)).

## Output

Print the only integer — the number of garlands modulo $*p*$.

## Note

In the first sample the following variants are possible: 121|1|12, 121|1|21, 121|2|12, 121|2|21, 212|1|12, 212|1|21, 212|2|12, 212|2|21. In the second sample the following variants are possible: 12|13, 12|23, 12|31, 12|32 and so on.

Figure for the first sample: ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/85a10fec7ccb1539cd891c6208ebac9368cab9ee.png)
statementZhMd:
由于 Gerald、Alexander、Sergey 和 Gennady 已经忙于通常的新年事务，Edward 匆忙地装饰着新年树。任何像样的新年树都必须挂上一条漂亮的彩灯串。Edward 有 $*m*$ 种颜色的灯，他想用这些灯组成一条彩灯串。这条彩灯串应表示一个长度为 $*L*$ 的序列。Edward 的树有 $*n*$ 层，他计划这样悬挂彩灯串：第一层使用前 $*l*_{1}$ 盏灯，第二层使用接下来的 $*l*_{2}$ 盏灯，依此类推。最后的第 $*n*$ 层使用最后的 $*l*_{*n*}$ 盏灯，![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e444352e6f3188286a54650b0cc918121525a492.png)

Edward 喜欢各种数学谜题，因此他突然想知道：在满足以下两个条件的情况下，共有多少种不同的彩灯串组成方式：

1. 同一层中任意两盏相邻的灯颜色必须不同。
2. 任意两个**相邻**层中所使用的颜色集合必须不同。我们考虑无序集合（而不是多重集合），其中每种颜色至多出现一次。因此，某种颜色的灯使用了多少盏并不重要。

请帮助 Edward 找出这个困扰他的问题的答案，否则他将无法在新年之前装饰好这棵树。你可以认为每种颜色的灯都有无限多盏，并且不要求使用全部 $*m*$ 种颜色。如果将彩灯串表示为序列后，至少有一个位置不同，则认为两条彩灯串不同。请输出答案对 $*p*$ 取模后的结果。

## 输入格式

第一行包含三个整数 $*n*$、$*m*$ 和 $*p*$（$1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 10^{6}$，$2 ≤ *p* ≤ 10^{9}$），分别表示树的层数、灯的颜色数以及模数。下一行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*l*_{*i}$（$1 ≤ *l*_{*i} ≤ 5000$，![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ba00472aa4924de40da7f039202523b7f0cf35f8.png)）。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——彩灯串数量对 $*p*$ 取模后的结果。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，以下方案是可行的：121|1|12、121|1|21、121|2|12、121|2|21、212|1|12、212|1|21、212|2|12、212|2|21。在第二个样例中，以下方案是可行的：12|13、12|23、12|31、12|32 等。

第一个样例的图示：![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/85a10fec7ccb1539cd891c6208ebac9368cab9ee.png)
